brief.topic: What Changes When You Keep the Better of Two Draws?

s01: Draw a number from one through four, all equally likely.
Its average is two and a half.
Now draw twice independently and keep the larger number.
What is the new average?
There are sixteen equally likely ordered pairs.
Each cell in this grid is one pair.
Write the larger of its row and column numbers in the cell.
Only one cell has maximum one.
Three have maximum two.
Five have maximum three.
Seven have maximum four.
Why the odd counts?
A maximum at most two means both draws lie in the first two choices.
That gives a two by two square.
Expanding from a square of side k minus one to side k adds two k minus one cells.
Weight each possible maximum by its count.
One times one, two times three, three times five, and four times seven.
Fifty, divided by sixteen.
The new average is three point one two five.
It is larger because the rule discards the smaller draw, not because either individual draw changed.
If we copy the first draw instead of making an independent second draw, only the four diagonal cells remain possible.
Their maximum is just the original draw.
The average returns to two and a half.
Two opportunities help differently when they are really the same opportunity.

scenes.narration:
Draw a number from one through four, all equally likely. Its average is two and a half. Now draw twice independently and keep the larger number. What is the new average?

There are sixteen equally likely ordered pairs. Each cell in this grid is one pair. Write the larger of its row and column numbers in the cell.

Only one cell has maximum one. Three have maximum two. Five have maximum three. Seven have maximum four.

Why the odd counts? A maximum at most two means both draws lie in the first two choices. That gives a two by two square. Expanding from a square of side k minus one to side k adds two k minus one cells.

Weight each possible maximum by its count. One times one, two times three, three times five, and four times seven. Fifty, divided by sixteen. The new average is three point one two five.

It is larger because the rule discards the smaller draw, not because either individual draw changed.

If we copy the first draw instead of making an independent second draw, only the four diagonal cells remain possible. Their maximum is just the original draw. The average returns to two and a half. Two opportunities help differently when they are really the same opportunity.
